record.question: She has not seen him for several days.
record.explanation: The PDF underlines several, not for. Several modifies the plural noun days and expresses an indefinite number. Adjective is the supplied traditional classification; Merriam-Webster explicitly labels this use an adjective and gives a several days example. Some modern grammars call it a determiner, which is not an offered option. Preposition would classify the different, non-underlined word for. Verified solution (unofficial); reviewed 26 October 2026. References: https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/several
record.direction: Direction (Question Nos. 51 - 55) : Choose the correct parts of speech for the underlined word from the given alternatives:
record.questionMarkup: She has not seen him for __several__ days.
